1.explanation: All of the REST-specific syntax definitions live in components/prism-rest.js (and its minified counterpart). This is where Prism’s patterns for literal text (``…``), hyperlinks (<…>_), emphasis, and other inline-markup are registered and ordered. The bug — failure to match a <link>_ immediately adjacent to a literal block and the fallback to emphasis — is caused by the way those patterns are defined and inserted in this file. Editing prism-rest.js to adjust the regex ordering or lookaround logic (and then regenerating the minified file) is required to fix the issue.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting reStructuredText containing an inline link immediately followed by an underscore reference marker (e.g. ``<https://...>_``) and an adjacent ```` literal (e.g. ````ALTER_ROLE````), Prism’s REST grammar fails to detect the link or the back-tick literal correctly. Instead the entire sequence is consumed by the italic (emphasis) rule and rendered as a single italic span. If the link and the literal are separated into two lines, each is highlighted correctly.

2.explanation: The reST language definition lives in prism-rest.js (and its minified version). It provides regex patterns for links, inline literals, and emphasis. When link and literal syntax appear together on one line, the current pattern order or look‐around logic consumes them as a single emphasis token. Fixing requires adjusting the regex definitions or token order in prism-rest.js so that links and inline code are detected before emphasis.
2.bug_scenario: When a single line of reStructuredText contains both an inline hyperlink (``<URL>``_) and inline literal text (````code````) Prism’s REST grammar fails to recognize either token and instead wraps the entire span in emphasis. Splitting the link and literal onto separate lines works correctly, showing that the fault lies in how links and verbatim literals are tokenized when adjacent on the same line.
